classification.difficultyReason: Apply the vertical line test to six supplied graphs and illustrate a repeated input.

content.prompt: In each case, copy the graph, then draw a vertical line to show that the graph does not represent a function.

spec.description: Circle centred at the origin with all four intercept labels; no grid.

answer.short: Draw the vertical line $x=0$; it meets the circle at $(0,3)$ and $(0,-3)$.
answer.worked: Copy the circle and use the $y$-axis as the vertical test line. The input $x=0$ has two outputs, $3$ and $-3$, so the relation is not a function.

spec.description: The y-axis is the selected vertical test line; intersection markers distinguish it from the ordinary axis.
Left semicircle, closed endpoints, labelled axes and positive x tick; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Left half of radius-2 circle centred at origin.

answer.worked: Copy the semicircle and use the $y$-axis as the vertical test line. Both endpoints are included, so the input $x=0$ has outputs $2$ and $-2$. The relation is not a function.

spec.description: Vertical test line on the y-axis through both included endpoints.
Schematic sideways S curve with three y-axis crossings and arrows at its outward ends. Bézier geometry preserves the supplied shape without asserting an equation or horizontal scale.

answer.short: Draw $x=0$; it meets the curve at $y=-2,0,2$.
answer.worked: Copy the curve and use the $y$-axis as the vertical test line. The input $x=0$ has three outputs, $-2$, $0$ and $2$, so the relation is not a function.

spec.description: Y-axis test line with three intersection markers.
Left-opening parabola with vertex (4,0), y-intercepts ±2 and arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Equation-driven reconstruction x=4−y²; equation is not printed.

answer.worked: Copy the parabola and use the $y$-axis as the vertical test line. The input $x=0$ gives both $y=2$ and $y=-2$, so the relation is not a function.

spec.description: Y-axis test line through both y-intercepts.
Two schematic curves symmetric about both axes, with upper minimum (0,1), lower maximum (0,−1) and four outward arrows. No equation is asserted.

answer.worked: Copy both curves and use the $y$-axis as the vertical test line. It meets the upper curve at $(0,1)$ and the lower curve at $(0,-1)$. One input has two outputs, so the relation is not a function.

spec.description: Y-axis test line through the two turning points.
Schematic vertical loop reaching y=3, crossing itself at the origin, with two lower tails approaching the dashed line y=−1. No equation or horizontal scale is asserted.
spec.mathematics: The y-axis meets the relation at (0,0) and (0,3); dashed horizontal asymptote y=−1.

answer.worked: Copy the loop and its lower branches, retaining the dashed line $y=-1$. Use the $y$-axis as the vertical test line: it meets the curve at the origin and the top of the loop. The input $x=0$ has outputs $0$ and $3$, so the relation is not a function.

spec.description: Y-axis test line through the origin and loop maximum.
